title: Frontend & User Interface Foundations
description: Understand how browser applications work and build accessible interactions with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, state, and API requests.

lessons.title: Browser and web basics
lessons.principle: A browser requests resources over HTTP(S), parses HTML, styles with CSS, and executes JavaScript within security boundaries.
lessons.practice: Sketch what happens when a user navigates to an application URL.

lessons.title: Identify the runtime boundary
lessons.principle: The browser is user-controlled and cannot securely enforce secrets or final permission checks.
lessons.practice: Move authoritative validation and protected operations to an appropriate trusted backend.

lessons.title: Semantic HTML
lessons.principle: Semantic elements give documents and controls meaning beyond their visual appearance.
lessons.practice: Build a page using main, headings, labels, buttons, and lists for their intended purposes.

lessons.title: Choose proper interactive elements
lessons.principle: Buttons perform actions, anchors navigate, and labels name inputs.
lessons.practice: Avoid click handlers on arbitrary div elements when a native button can do the job.

lessons.title: CSS foundations
lessons.principle: Selectors, cascade, box model, and layout rules determine presentation without changing document semantics.
lessons.practice: Style a simple card with predictable class selectors and responsive widths.

lessons.title: Inspect layout issues systematically
lessons.principle: Padding, border, margin, overflow, and positioning often explain apparent alignment defects.
lessons.practice: Use browser computed styles and box-model tools instead of random CSS overrides.

lessons.title: JavaScript in the browser
lessons.principle: JavaScript reads and updates document state through DOM APIs and event listeners.
lessons.practice: Attach a click listener that safely changes visible task text.

lessons.title: Prefer safe DOM updates
lessons.principle: Injecting untrusted strings into HTML can enable script injection.
lessons.practice: Set textContent for plain text and sanitize trusted rich-content workflows when HTML is unavoidable.

lessons.title: Forms and validation
lessons.principle: Form controls gather values, require labels, and need visible feedback for invalid submission.
lessons.practice: Make an add-task form that trims text and blocks empty submissions.

lessons.title: Preserve submission semantics
lessons.principle: Enter key, submit event, pending state, and error feedback are part of a usable form.
lessons.practice: Handle submit rather than only button click; keep entered data when validation or save fails.

lessons.title: UI state and rendering
lessons.principle: UI state determines what a user sees; rendering should reflect the latest authoritative data.
lessons.practice: Model a loading, empty, ready, saving, and error state.

lessons.title: Avoid race-condition displays
lessons.principle: A slower previous request can overwrite the result of a newer request.
lessons.practice: Track request identity or cancel obsolete requests before updating visible results.

lessons.title: Asynchronous network requests
lessons.principle: fetch returns a promise and responses may fail at transport, protocol, or application layers.
lessons.practice: Check response.ok, parse the expected body, and handle timeout or cancellation as applicable.

lessons.title: Differentiate error states
lessons.principle: HTTP 404, network disconnection, invalid JSON, and business-validation errors require different responses.
lessons.practice: Provide user-actionable messages without implying that every non-2xx response is a disconnected network.

lessons.title: Accessibility fundamentals
lessons.principle: People must be able to perceive, understand, navigate, and operate the interface with varied abilities and devices.
lessons.practice: Test keyboard focus, heading order, labels, status messages, and color contrast.

lessons.title: Avoid keyboard traps
lessons.principle: A modal or custom widget must preserve usable focus order and Escape behavior when appropriate.
lessons.practice: Prefer native dialog and controls where possible and manually test with keyboard-only navigation.

lessons.title: Responsive and mobile UX
lessons.principle: Responsive design adapts layout to viewport and input method, not just device labels.
lessons.practice: Start with a narrow layout and expand only when content needs more space.

lessons.title: Support touch and text scaling
lessons.principle: Tiny targets and fixed-height containers can fail on phones and with larger text settings.
lessons.practice: Test long labels, zoom, orientation, tap-target spacing, and reduced motion as relevant.

lessons.title: Frontend verification
lessons.principle: Visible polish is not proof of correct data flow, accessibility, or failure handling.
lessons.practice: Test create-task, empty form, reload, slow network, and keyboard behavior.

lessons.title: Use AI to generate test ideas
lessons.principle: AI can propose scenarios but cannot replace observing the application in a real browser.
lessons.practice: Record screenshots or reproduction steps only as supporting evidence alongside functional checks.
